newsitem.title: UK: UK's Camelot looking to expand - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK's Camelot looking to expand - paper.

text.p: Britain's National Lottery operator Camelot Group Plc has held discussions with BSkyB, Ladbroke and Bass aimed at expanding its gaming interests, the Financial Times said on Thursday.
Quoting a leaked document, the newspaper said the most detailed talks were with brewing and leisure group Bass over the formation of an 80-number lottery game called "Keno".
But the game, which could have been transmitted to pubs and restaurants, was thought to have been turned down by Oflot, the National Lottery regulator.
Talks with Ladbroke were said by the newspaper to have involved linking the Vernons pools business with Camelot's network of lottery terminals.
In separate talks, Camelot was said to be discussing using BSkyB's satellite television technology to allow people to buy lottery tickets via their tv screens.
Camelot confirmed to the newspaper that the leaked material was genuine but stressed "there is a world of difference between such brainstorming of ideas and adopting them as company policy".
The Financial Times said Camelot was considering inviting other countries to "tag-on" to Britain's national lottery.
